question: Should this PR establish `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.hostnameAllowlist` as a web_fetch-only security contract now, or should hostname/domain egress policy wait for the broader egress/proxy direction?
rationale: This is not just implementation plumbing: operators may rely on the new config as an outbound data-exfiltration boundary, and related open work proposes different ownership models for fetch, providers, search, and managed proxy routing.

options.title: Accept Narrow web_fetch Contract
options.body: Approve `hostnameAllowlist` as a web_fetch-only opt-in policy, then rebase and validate this PR before merge.

options.title: Fold Into Shared Egress Policy
options.body: Pause this PR and define one cross-tool domain policy for fetch, search, browser/provider fallback, cache, redirects, and proxy routing first.

options.title: Wait For Managed Proxy Direction
options.body: Keep this PR as comparison material until the managed-proxy PR is accepted or rejected as the owner boundary for app-owned egress.

recommendation.title: Accept Narrow web_fetch Contract
recommendation.body: Approve `hostnameAllowlist` as a web_fetch-only opt-in policy, then rebase and validate this PR before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history across the web_fetch runtime, SSRF helpers, docs/config surface, and repository ownership signals involved in this security-boundary choice.
